entries.what_happened: One manuscript, “The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable” (dated September 23, 2026), claims that every colouring of the Euclidean plane with five colours has a monochromatic unit-distance pair, with no regularity assumption on the colour classes. Its main theorem (thm:main) states that the plane has no proper five-colouring even when arbitrary colour classes are allowed, and so 6 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7. The upper bound 7 is the classical hexagonal colouring (Hadwiger 1961), which the paper reproduces; the new content is the lower bound 6. The argument has two parts. (1) Transfer (thm:transfer, with Proposition palettes-forward and a density-point converse): for every positive integer k, a proper k-colouring of the plane exists if and only if a “weak measurable” k-colouring exists. A weak measurable colouring is a Lebesgue-measurable colouring in which same-coloured unit pairs have zero measure in the product of plane Lebesgue measure and normalised arc length on the circle. The forward direction averages a proper colouring over the algebraic plane, projects onto the continuous factor by conditional expectation, and uses a rigidity theorem (thm:rigidity: every K-invariant probability on the character group with zero mass on the ordinary continuous characters is Haar). The converse uses density points and de Bruijn–Erdős compactness. (2) Theorem weak-five (no weak measurable five-colouring): the paper builds angular palettes at each centre with at most two labels (prop:palette-size), shows that the centres whose transition graph contains a cycle form a locally finite set (thm:cyclic-local-finiteness), extracts a label cycle of length 3, 4 or 5 with compact connected exclusion sets (prop:interface-cycle), and excludes each cycle length by an angular argument (prop:angular-five, prop:angular-four, prop:angular-three). The three-cycle case uses a rational placement certificate for seven points forming a Moser-spindle-type configuration (lem:angular-certificate). A corollary (cor:positive-badness) also states, as a consequence, that a finite unit-distance graph is not five-colourable, with an existential positive constant for the monochromatic-pair frequency.
entries.delivers: For the list's problem, the claim establishes the lower bound χ(ℝ²) ≥ 6: there is no proper five-colouring of the plane, with arbitrary colour classes, in ZFC. Together with the known seven-colouring it gives 6 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7, which moves the lower bound from the known 5 to 6. This is the list's part (1). For part (2), the claim gives only an existential finite statement: by de Bruijn–Erdős compactness there is a finite unit-distance graph that is not five-colourable, so its chromatic number is at least 6. The paper does not display this graph, and gives no size or explicit construction. The paper's statement of the problem matches the list's: the plane, distance exactly one, no regularity on the colour classes. The paper does not claim to settle the problem. Its introduction says the alternatives six and seven remain unresolved. Part (3) of the list's problem statement, covering other distances, dimensions other than two, and fractional or density versions, is not addressed.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, χ(ℝ²) is either 6 or 7, and which one holds is open. The paper's footnote mentions a May 14, 2026 manuscript of Reed that claims χ(ℝ²) = 7. The paper says that manuscript's displayed theorem assumes the key density bound as a hypothesis, so it does not establish 7; this is context, not part of this family's claim. Also open: whether six colours suffice (a 6-colouring of the plane would be needed for the lower bound to be sharp), an explicit finite unit-distance graph with chromatic number at least 6 (the paper's graph is existential and of unknown size), and the list's variants with other distances, other dimensions, or fractional and density versions.
entries.direction: proves a lower bound: χ(ℝ²) ≥ 6, improving the known lower bound 5
entries.object: None for the lower bound. Non-five-colourability is proved by contradiction. The finite unit-distance graph in cor:positive-badness is obtained by compactness and is not displayed. The seven-colouring in the proof of thm:main (hexagonal, from Hadwiger 1961) is explicit, but it is the known upper bound, not a new object.
entries.conditional_on: The main theorem assumes nothing beyond ZFC. It cites standard results: the abelian spectral theorem and Bochner's theorem, the Følner criterion for amenable groups, Fourier uniqueness, and de Bruijn–Erdős compactness. Corollary cor:positive-badness part (i) depends on Gwyn and Stavrianos 2020 (Lemma 2.10 and Theorem 2.11), and part (ii) depends on Bourgeat, Heinrich, Melotti and Robert 2015 (Theorems 1–2) for its needle-frequency bounds. The paper cites Sokolov–Voronov 2025 and Voronov 2025 as precedents for its interface and strip arguments, not as steps it relies on.
entries.doubts: (1) Length and compression: the argument spans about 4,600 lines of LaTeX across eight section files, and the abstract and introduction give only an outline. The interface-cycle construction (prop:interface-cycle) is summarised in an overview paragraph (“A planar cover obstruction forces a nontrivial loop…”), and the caption of its exclusion figure calls the shape “schematic”. I read that proposition's statement and the start of its section only. (2) The seven-point certificate (lem:angular-certificate) is verified by tables of decimal coordinate boxes, polynomial bounds and residual numerators, and the text calls this a rational verification. I read that verification but did not recheck its arithmetic. (3) I did not read the relative-singularity and multiple-averages lemmas in rigidity.tex, nor the middle parts of palettes.tex, transitions.tex, interfaces.tex and angular.tex. My account of them rests on the introduction's outline and the statements I did read. (4) The bounds in cor:positive-badness part (ii) are imported from Bourgeat et al. by citation, and the constant δ = 1/m is non-constructive. I found no inconsistency between the abstract and thm:main.
